text:
Maya Chen: thinking through multi-tenant telemetry isolation — want to prototypetwo options and get opinions: per-tenant namespaces (separate indices/datasets) vs shared dataset with RBAC/tagging. main concerns: query perf, cardinality, retention enforcement, and dashboard UX.
Kevin Patel: fwiw per-tenant namespaces simplifies RBAC and retention, but cardinality explosion + higher storage costs. quick wins: soft quota + lifecycle policies.
Olga Sokolova: agree. also dashboard UX: ops teams need a simple tenant selector that scopes queries, not 20 different dashboards.
Raj Menon: +1. If we go shared, we must guarantee tenant_id is in all indexed fields AND enforce query scoping at gateway to avoid accidental cross-tenant leaks.
Emily Rivera: curious about exporter-level routing — can we tag spans at ingestion and route heavy customers to a dedicated exporter/namespace? that limits noisy neighbor risk.
Maya Chen: exactly. prototype idea: otel collector/ingest pipeline looks at resource.attributes.tenant_id -> route to dataset X. fallback to shared if missing. minimal pressure on query layer.
Kevin Patel: cost analysis: if 1000 tenants and 5% high volume -> we'd create ~50 dedicated namespaces. ok. autoscale for exporters. but small tenants in shared keep costs low.
Olga Sokolova: one challenge: cross-tenant traces for internal debugging (service-to-service across accounts). if totally siloed, devs lose ability to trace multi-tenant interactions. need a safe bypass with audit logs.
Raj Menon: propose RBAC model: per-namespace read/write for customer teams, plus internal svc account with explicit allowlist for cross-tenant debugging; all bypass ops logged to audit stream.
Emily Rivera: retention enforcement — implement a policy engine in ingest that attaches retention_ttl and enforces via lifecycle manager. stash policy per-tenant in tenant-metadata store.
Maya Chen: sketch of pipeline rule: 
```
if resource.attributes.tenant_id in heavy_tenant_list:
  route := tenant_namespace(tenant_id)
else:
  route := shared_namespace
set retention := tenant_policy.ttl
```
We'd store heavy_tenant_list from pricing/contract system.
Kevin Patel: also need quotas at ingestion throttle level. OTEL collector -> rate limiter plugin keyed by tenant_id.
Olga Sokolova: dashboard UX: instead of N dashboards, build single template with tenant variable that swaps datasource and dashboard filters. makes rollout easier.
Raj Menon: ops question: how do we handle historical data when we move a tenant from shared -> namespace? reindexing is expensive.
Maya Chen: prefer routing new data to new namespace and keep shared historical read-only with a mapped alias for queries during transition. deprecate alias after retention window.
sre-bot: incident-notice: latency spike seen last week correlated with heavy exporter fanout for 3 customers. tagging those tenants for dedicated routing would have helped. :rotating_light:
Emily Rivera: actionable: I can prototype collector routing + rate-limiter in a sandbox. Kevin, can you run a cost projection for 50 dedicated namespaces vs shared retention bump?
Kevin Patel: yes. will have numbers by EOD Thu.
Maya Chen: plan: Emily prototype, Kevin cost, Raj defines RBAC bypass + audit requirements, Olga prototypes dashboard variable template. sync next Tues 10am. :thumbsup:
